summary: An array that should contain 1..n has one value duplicated in place of another; return [duplicate, missing].
mainInsight: Count how often each value 1..n appears: the value seen twice is the duplicate and the value seen zero times is the missing one. Equivalently, sum(nums) - sum(set(nums)) gives the duplicate and n(n+1)/2 - sum(set(nums)) the missing value.
invariant: After the counting pass, count[v] is the number of times v occurs; exactly one v has count 2 and exactly one has count 0.

approaches.name: Sort and scan
approaches.summary: Sort; adjacent equal values give the duplicate, a gap gives the missing value.
weaknesses: Edge handling when the missing value is 1 or n

approaches.name: Counting array
approaches.summary: count[v] for v in 1..n; find the 2 and the 0.

approaches.name: Sum with a set
approaches.summary: dup = sum(nums) - sum(set(nums)); missing = n(n+1)/2 - sum(set(nums)).

approaches.name: Sign marking in place
approaches.summary: For each |v| negate nums[|v| - 1]; an already-negative slot means v is the duplicate; the positive slot is the missing value.

personalSolution.approach: Sum of nums minus sum of set(nums) for the duplicate; Gauss sum minus sum of the set for the missing value
personalSolution.notes: Optimal time. The set makes it O(n) space; sign marking reaches O(1) extra space if asked.

commonMistakes: Assuming the duplicate and the missing value are adjacent numbers.
Returning [missing, duplicate] in the wrong order.
With sort-and-scan, forgetting the missing value can be n (or 1).
edgeCases: Duplicate far from the missing value, e.g. [2, 2, 3, 4] style inputs.

cards.answer: A slot already negative means v was seen before
cards.explanation: Use index v - 1 as v's 'seen' flag. Hitting an already-negative slot gives the duplicate; after the pass, the one slot still positive is at index missing - 1.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A negative slot means its index is the m: Reversed: the positive slot left at the end points to the missing value.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Negative values reveal which elements ar: All values are within 1..n by construction.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Signs record which half of the range has: That is a binary-search idea, not what sign marking does.

promptVariants: Explain why each line of your solution gives the right number.
Why does sum(nums) - sum(set(nums)) equal the duplicate?
cards.answer: set(nums) keeps one copy of each value, so it is 1..n minus the missing value. sum(nums) has the duplicate counted twice, so the difference is exactly the duplicate. n(n+1)/2 is the sum of 1..n, so subtracting the set sum leaves the missing value.
keyPoints: Set removes exactly one copy of the duplicate
Gauss sum minus the set sum is the missing value
cards.explanation: Two aggregates of the same data, each missing one different thing, isolate the two unknowns.
cards.code:
totalWithDup = sum(nums)
totalWithoutDup = sum(set(nums))
n = len(nums)
dup = totalWithDup - totalWithoutDup
missing = n * (n + 1) // 2 - totalWithoutDup
return [dup, missing]

promptVariants: Why doesn't sum(range(1, n + 1)) - sum(nums) alone answer the problem?

options: missing - duplicate: one equation, two unknowns

cards.answer: missing - duplicate: one equation, two unknowns
cards.explanation: The duplicate replaced the missing value, so the sums differ by missing - dup. You need a second equation (set sum, sum of squares, or counts).

incorrectOptionExplanations.The duplicate, since it was counted twic: The difference mixes both numbers; it is missing - duplicate.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The missing value, as in Missing Number: In Missing Number nothing replaced it; here the duplicate distorts the sum.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Zero, because the lengths are equal: Equal length does not mean equal sums; it is zero only if missing == dup.
